To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the peptides released from amaranth proteins after gastrointestinal digestion have antihypertension effects and that the emulsification of amaranth peptides enhances the antihypotensive effect of these peptides in vivo.

the peptides derived from amaranth proteins exert a blood pressure-lowering effect in SHR, acting on the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), and that the peptides are protected from gastrointestinal digestion when they are incorporated into a food matrix.
the amaranth proteins and its peptides are a good source of ACE inhibitors and that they can be used as an ingredient to develop new functional foods to treat high blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a functional food with a high content of peptides that are able to regulate the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) and, consequently, to reduce blood pressure.
the study of the effect of amaranths proteins/peptides on the RAS.
the development of new functional foods for the treatment of high blood pressure, which could be used in a complementary or alternative way to pharmacological treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peptides derived from the amaranth protein exert a hypotensive effect on SHR.

the amaranth protein hydrolysates and the peptides generated after GID have a hypotensive effect, and this effect could be due to their ability to act on the plasma ACE, plasma Renin and the vascular endothelium.

the amaranth protein hydrolysate and the emulsion with this hydrolysate (GE+VIKPs) have a significant hypotensive effect in SHR, and the mechanism of this effect involves the inhibition of ACE, the inhibition of renin, and the relaxation of the vascular system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
amaranth peptides are effective in the regulation of blood pressure in SHR.
we found a new source of antihypertension peptides, which are able to reduce the systolic blood pressure in SHR.
amaranth protein and its hydrolysates have a potential antihypertensives effect, which is mediated by the inhibition of the renin-angiotensin system and the vasodilatory effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emulsions can protect bioactive peptides from gastrointestinal digestion, and that the peptides released after digestion have antihypertension properties.
the use of emulsions as a protection against gastrointestinal digestion can be a strategy to improve the bioavailability of peptides with antihypertension activity.

the use of amarnath protein/peptides as a food ingredient may be a promising approach for the management of hypertension, and that the emulsion system used in this work is a promising strategy to protect bioactive peptides against gastrointestinal digestion and to improve their bioavailability.
